PAGE_3:
NEXT LEVEL WEBSITE CONTENT – ACTION GUIDE 
  IAPWE Professional Development Series 3 How to Use Your Action Guide   You’ll get the best results from any course you participate in by completing the Action Steps at the end of each module. They will help you apply what you learn directly to your business and your life, maximizing the investment you’re making.  Use the following Action Guide to record your answers, insights, and other notes for the Action Steps, which are outlined in your Course Book. You’ll want to refer to each module’s content as you complete the related steps.  While we have left space in the guide for each action step, you may feel more comfortable using a separate notebook or digital application for your work. Use whatever method you feel most comfortable with and don’t feel constrained to using the space in the Action Guide alone.  In addition, your course may have other Action Sheets, such as spreadsheets or planning templates, which are separate from the guide. Look out for those with your other course materials.  Finally, you don’t have to complete all the steps at once. Instead, try setting a specific time on your calendar to work on them. And don’t feel that you have to get it right the first time. Learning is a process that happens as you apply your new skills and knowledge. You’ll want to return periodically to your Action Guide and both remind yourself of the work you’ve achieved and edit your answers as you see their impact.   Have fun with it and enjoy the progress and successes that will happen as a result of your work!

  IAPWE Professional Development Series 5 Module 1 – Laying the Foundation: Evaluate Your Target Audience & Content  1. Before you take your web content to the next level, it’s helpful to understand who your audience is and what kind of content they want. Reflect and write down answers to these questions: 
Who is your target audience? Focus on demographics, psychographics, and online behavior.

PAGE_6:
NEXT LEVEL WEBSITE CONTENT – ACTION GUIDE 
  IAPWE Professional Development Series 6 What are some of the problems or issues your customer base has expressed?  
What subjects are they passionate about?  
What causes or organizations do they identify with?

PAGE_7:
NEXT LEVEL WEBSITE CONTENT – ACTION GUIDE 
  IAPWE Professional Development Series 7 2. Analyze what has worked for you in the past and apply these learnings to future content. Review your social media and blog posts and pages with the most interactions or visits, and ask yourself: What do these pages and posts have in common?  
What questions did the content answer?  
What comments stand out?

NEXT LEVEL WEBSITE CONTENT – ACTION GUIDE 
  IAPWE Professional Development Series 8 3. It will be easier to work with your sitemap if it's in a spreadsheet. To do this, convert the XML file you created into a CSV file using an online converter like onlinexmltools. Once the data is saved as a CSV file, it can easily be imported into Excel or other spreadsheet software. 4. Conduct your website review using your sitemap spreadsheet.  Highlight what to keep, redirect, or change/expand based on the step-by-step process in the module: Ø Identify essential pages Ø Check the competition  Ø Keep your target in mind  Ø Evaluate each page Use different colors for each to help with sorting and prioritizing which pages you want to work on first.  Notes

PAGE_9:
NEXT LEVEL WEBSITE CONTENT – ACTION GUIDE 
  IAPWE Professional Development Series 9 Module 2 – Rethink Your Website Design and Structure  1. Go to your home page and answer these questions: Currently, what is the dominant piece of information or image? Does it further your business goals?  
When people land on your home page, is it immediately apparent what you are selling or the services you offer?  
Brainstorm ways that you can improve your home page

PAGE_10:
NEXT LEVEL WEBSITE CONTENT – ACTION GUIDE 
  IAPWE Professional Development Series 10 2. Reflect on your personal story and your brand's story and answer these questions: What sets you apart from the competition? Have you included this in your 'About Us' section?  
Is there another way to tell your story that would be more appealing to your target audience?  
Is all of the information in your About Us section necessary or does it distract the audience from your key messaging?

PAGE_11:
NEXT LEVEL WEBSITE CONTENT – ACTION GUIDE 
  IAPWE Professional Development Series 11 3. Is there anything on your essential pages that is there just because it's 'always been done that way' but doesn't contribute to your website goals? Consider removing graphics, photos, or content that doesn't add value.  Notes

  IAPWE Professional Development Series 12 Module 3 – Incorporate Long-Form Content into Your Website   1. Reflect on your business goals, and list 5 ways that long-form content can further these goals.  1  2  3  4  5

  IAPWE Professional Development Series 13 2. Following the instructions in this module, create or update your list of keywords for your website, using free resources such as UberSuggest. Set aside these keywords for future use.  Notes 
 3. Use the Idea Bank spreadsheet to record five long-form content ideas, include 'post/article type' if it applies (e.g. Epic List, Ultimate Guide etc.) and any keywords that might be related to this topic. Don't worry: you're at the idea generation stage. You are not committed to anything that you add to the Idea Bank. You will revisit and update the Idea Bank as you work your way through the course (and after you complete it!)

NEXT LEVEL WEBSITE CONTENT – ACTION GUIDE 
  IAPWE Professional Development Series 14 4. Brainstorm who can help you create long-form content – an assistant, freelancer, partner, or even crowd-sourcing with your customers. Based on your answers, you will need to budget time (and possibly money) for these increased content demands. If you have a potential writer for any of the 5 topics you brainstormed, add them to the Idea Bank now.  Who Can Help? How to Contact

PAGE_15:
NEXT LEVEL WEBSITE CONTENT – ACTION GUIDE 
  IAPWE Professional Development Series 15 Module 4 – Three Long-Form Content Strategies to Boost Site Ranking and Visits  1. Review the three long-form content strategies presented in this module and determine which strategy (or strategies) would work best for you. It could be one or all three, depending on your topic ideas. audience, and goals.    Pillar  Skyscraper  Ladder    2. Revisit your Idea Bank and review the topics you have already brainstormed. Do any stand out as Pillar, Skyscraper, or Ladder content? Make notes on each.

PAGE_16:
NEXT LEVEL WEBSITE CONTENT – ACTION GUIDE 
  IAPWE Professional Development Series 16 Pillar Take a look at the keywords related each topic you brainstormed. Are any of the keywords similar (or identical) to the topic idea? This is a good indicator that this topic would work well as Pillar content. If so, label the idea as Pillar content, brainstorm ideas around possible subtopics (Clusters), and look for copy that already exists on your website that you can also link to.

PAGE_17:
NEXT LEVEL WEBSITE CONTENT – ACTION GUIDE 
  IAPWE Professional Development Series 17 Skyscraper Have any of your topic ideas already been written about online and you know you could do a better job, offering more comprehensive information? This could be great Skyscraper content.

PAGE_18:
NEXT LEVEL WEBSITE CONTENT – ACTION GUIDE 
  IAPWE Professional Development Series 18 Ladder Are any of your topic ideas very current, time limited, and relevant to your business or industry? (e.g. The Ultimate List of Social Media Marketing Conferences This Year!). Consider developing it into Ladder content.

PAGE_19:
NEXT LEVEL WEBSITE CONTENT – ACTION GUIDE 
  IAPWE Professional Development Series 19 3. Now that you've learned about three different types of content, use the Idea Bank Spreadsheet to brainstorm 5 more Pillar, Skyscraper, and Ladder content ideas. Label each as either Pillar, Skyscraper, or Ladder' under 'Content Type'.  Notes

  IAPWE Professional Development Series 20 4. Refer back to your audience information from Module 1 and your business goals from Module 3, to make sure your ideas appeal to your audience and further your goals.
